cells.remarks: Issued from Mānyakhēţa. Records the tax-free grant, made by the king, of the village Lōhagrāma situated in Rāmapurī- 700 to Kēśava-dīkshita, the son of Dāmodara-bhaţţa, who hailed from Pundravardhana-nagara, and who belonged to the Kauśika-gōtra and Vājasanēya-śākhā, for the king's own merit as well as for the merit of his parents. The boundaries of the gift-village are stated to be Ghōdgēgrāma in the east, Vamjūlīgrāma in the south, Vīmcha-vihārabharāma in the west and Sōnātīgrāma in the north. Published in Ind. Ant., Vol. XII, p. 247 f. and plate.

cells.place: No. 4. (Museum Acc. No. 495).
cells.remarks: Records the royal gift of the village nava-kāna-alias Veṅkaṭama-hārayāpuram in Nārāyaṇapura-pattu in Kunthavatī-kōṭṭam of Ninra-nādu in Chandragiri-rājya to Pratiśādi-bhayaṁkara Annagāchārya, who was the son of Nainār and the grandson of Veṅkaṭāchārya, of Vatsa-gotra, Āpastamba-sūtra and Yajus-sākhā and well-versed in the Vedas, Śāstras and in the Vaiśhṇavāgama-siddhāntas. The composer of the record was Rāma-kavi, son of Kāmakōṭi and grandson of Sabhāpati and the writer was Achyutarārya, the son of Gauapārya and grandson of Viraṇāchārya.

cells.place: No. 6. (Museum Acc. No. 1352).
cells.remarks: States in Telugu that it is a copy of two earlier grants got engraved by Sēni-sēți of Penugonda. The first of the two grants in Kannada seems to pertain to the gift of land made by the Vaiśyas of Nidigallu for worship and offerings to god Nagarésvara in the fortress of Nidigallu in Saka 1111, Kilaka, Jyēshṭha śu. 5, Thursday (irregular), during the reign of Irungōla-chōla-mahārāja ruling from Nidigallu. The second inscription states that there arose a dispute regarding the right over the said temple and that in Saka 1616, Bhāva, Jyēshṭha śu. 5, Thursday (irregular), the chief Mummidi Hottaḷa-nāyaka of the locality confirmed the right over the Nagarēśvara temple in favour of the body called the Hundred-twenty belonging to the Nandēśvara aicatūru-llu, in accordance with the decision taken by the Śiṅgēri-svāmi and other scholars on the basis of the earlier record of the time of Irungōla-chōla-mahārāja. In late characters.

cells.remarks: Nandi Incomplete and seems to be spurious. Records the royal grant of the village Karihādāra-grāma situated in Tagaranāda-sīmā, to two brāhmaṇas named Raṅgahaṭṭa and Giribhaṭṭa, the sons of Vithala and the grandsons of Dattibhaṭṭa, belonging to Āpastamba-sūtra and Harīta-gōtra, as sarvamānya. cells.date: Śaka 1351 (pravardhamāna-vijaya-rājya-saṁvatsara), Saumya, Bhādrapada śu. 15, Monday, lunar eclipse=1429 A.D., September 12. (The month was Nija-Bhādrapada).
cells.remarks: Do. Issued from Udayagiri-nagara to the south of Śrīśaila in the presence of the deity Mātāṅgiramauli. Registers the royal grant of the village Mātāṅgahaṭṭi, as an agrahāra, situated to the north-east of Kudakupura, which is situated to the north of Barahakanyāpura in the Taulava country, together with its aṣṭa-bhōgayā, to Vishṇupūrvājña, the son of Śrīdhara and the grandson of Vishnu-vajvā, belonging to Kāśyapa-ānvaya and Yajub-śākhā. Refers to the deity Jyōti-liṅga-Mahēśvara-Siyarāṁbiu-Kōpīnātha of Kuḍakupura.

cells.location: Kommaralīngam, Udumalpet Taluk, Coimbatore District. Impressions through Shri P. R. Srinivasan. — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Incomplete Copper-plate set preserved in the same Museum.
cells.date: Phālguna ba. 15, Sunday, Rēvati, solar eclipse.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records the grant made by Bhūpati, the governor of Draviḍa country, of the village, Nēvāyi situated in Tuṇḍīra-maṇḍala as an agrahāra to Vāmana, the son of Gōvinda-yajvā, who belonged to Bhāradvāja-kula and who had studied the three Vēdas. Spurious (?). Second plate missing. Issued from his victorious camp Kittipūra (Kittipura). Records the grant of some villages to some brāhmaṇas. The grant was made with the permission of Cheramāna. In characters of about the 9th century A.D. Noticed in Kielhorn's Southern List, No. 1016. See also Indian Culture, Vol. III, pp. 303 ff.; Published in Ind. Ant., Vol. XVIII, pp. 362 ff. and plates.

cells.remarks: Damaged. Contra., Progress Report of the Kannada Research Institute for 1953-57, p. 8.

cells.remarks: Do. Records the construction of a temple and the installation of a linga at Indanūr by landprabhu Kalliaya who after laving the feet of the ascetic Annaiya-pandita of Sigguli made the grant of land and an oil mill for its upkeep, worship and feeding of ascetics. cells.remarks: Registers the gift of the village Kiriya Hingalige, a baḍa of Palambi-70 to the deities Ōmkārēśvara and Bagalēśvara-dēva and towards the maintenance, feeding of ascetics and etc., by mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Singarasa who was administering Hanungul-500 along with pergade Nūtimayya and Kēta-gāvunda after obtaining the consent of [Ma]lapa-dēva and by pergade Íśvarayya, Rāchamalla and Kēta-gāvunda after obtaining the consent of mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Śāntivarma, the Kadamab chief. cells.location: Kottalli
cells.place: Hero-stone standing on a hill-slope near a ruined Śiva temple.
cells.date: Chālukya Vikrama year 41, [Durmu*]-khi, Māgha śu. 10, Sunday = 1117 A.D., January 14, f.d.t. ·35.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records that while mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Tailapadēva was ruling over Banavāsi-12,000, Hanungal-500 and Haive-500, his close servant Kappeya-nāyaka, son of Toyimanāyaka of Koṭṭahalli died in a battle with Kāvadeva. The chief who along with pradhāna-daṇḍanayaka Masāṇayya and manē-verggade Saṅkarayya participated in the battle, appreciating his valour made grant of gaudaike and umbali to Boppa, the younger brother of the hero. Further records the performance of the marriage of Siriyabbe-nāyakiti, the daughter of Kappeya-nāyaka and Abbalabbe-nāyakiti by Sāṇteyadeva and Siriyadēvi. In characters of about the 12th century.

cells.place: Pedestal of the Hanuman image in the small shrine. Impression from the Superintending Archaeologist, western circle, Baroda.
cells.remarks: Worn out and impression incomplete. Noticed in A.R., Rājputāna Museum, 1917-18, p. 2; Bhandarkar's List, No. 177.

cells.place:
Another slab in the same Museum. Finds-
pot: Darā (Museum R. No. 31).
cells.date:
1906, Saka 1771, Pausha
ba. 5, Tuesday =
1849 A.D., Decem-
ber 4.
cells.remarks: Records that the chief went from Naṇḍagāon Koṭā to Mukun- darā for hunting a tiger which was killed and afterwards a great feast was given in the local palace. A function was held in which musicians participated, prizes were distributed and horses were provided with silver chains. The same day he entered Nandagāva where he honoured Bāvāgāra (i.e. chief priest) by presenting a shawl, a robe of honour and cash amount. Then he entered the palace and honoured his queen by giving presents and other festivities took place.

cells.date: Regnal year 7, Tamil Kanni 12, ba. 6, Rōhini, Sunday = 1324 A.D., September 9.
cells.remarks: Stones missing. Seems to record a transaction between the ūrār of Adhikaram in Suravī-nādu and Vānagarai alias Valudinārāyanadeva, the son of Sundarapāndya Vānagaraiyar, a servant of the royal palace, by receiving pāram from the latter, bestowing on him, in return, the proprietary right (kārāṇ-kīmāī-kāpu) of the land he had purchased in Kudikādu-Araśanēri, stipulating that he should remit certain taxes to the deity Akalankīsvaram-udaiyār. It is stated that the ūrār paid this money to the pērular in order to order to pay ānavindappagudi and viņdukkol to the deity (?) Amaṇādevar of that village.

cells.location: Tiruchchendurai
cells.place: Chandrasekharasvāmin temple, subhramandapa, east wall, outside.
cells.remarks: Damaged and partly built in. Seems to record the royal order issued at the instance of Toṇḍaimān, creating a taxfree devadāna out of specified lands in Jayangoṇḍa-śōḻanallūr, Tachchakuḍi and Kilinallūr, to be enjoyed by temples including those of the deities, Tirukkulīśanī-madēve, Tirumērkōvil-ālvar and ...da-viṇṇagar-ālvar from the 24th year of the king. Śuṅgan-tavirtarulina Kulōtuṅgachōla is also referred to. The lands are stated to have been given on lease to two persons one of whom is said to be Kulōtuṅgachōla-Vijayapālān of Perumarrūr. In characters of about the 13th century.

cells.place:
Śēndamangalam (otherwise known as
Śēndamaram).—Prahladēśvara temple,
mahāmaṇḍapa, east wall, outside.
cells.language: Tamil †
cells.remarks: Records the royal order issued to the authorities of the temple of the deity Puravarīsvaram-uḍaiya-nāyaṇār in Kallaga- nādu informing them of the exemption from taxes on the lands constituting tirumāṇikkāṇam purchased from the sabhaiyār of Sēndaṇ-brahmadēsam alias Puravarīchatur- vēdimangalam, a dēvadāna of Ālagapperumāl-viņṇagar- ālvar in Chuttavallichaturvēdimangalam. The lands were required to be colonised and named Kulasekharan-tiru- madaiyilgam after the king. Ayanguṟu tiru-uḍaiyāṇ alias Mā[lu]varāyan of Ayandūr alias Avidāyasundaranallūr in Tirukkāpparkkūṟram figures as one of the signatories. In characters of about the 13th century.

cells.remarks: Records an order of the state to the idaiyälar of the temple of the deity Välavalapädiya-İśvaramudaiyār at Kūpakaraiyānallūr in Tenkarai-nädu containing, as per the note (terippu) recorded on the copper-plate in the temple (tanjilkkoyil), details of the enumeration in terms of cooked rice (arisi-kkuţthiyu) various servants of the temple such as the Sivabrāhmaņas, unachchar and women servants (name given such as Kāmi alias Ālālasundara-māņikkam, Perumal alias Vēguvaņa- pperumāl-māņikkam etc.). These women did such work as required for tiruvangalai and tiruvandik-kippu for the deities viz., Tiruppaliyata-nâtchchiyar, Küttâduvar and Tambiräniyār, preparing the pastes for mañjakkappu, nellikkäppu and makkappu, stringing garlands, sweeping and washing the mahāmaņdapa and the first and second prākāras. Araiyan Viradamudittān alias Pallavarāyan of Chakkarapāņinallūr in Chevvirukkai- nādu figures as a signatory. In characters of the 13th century.

cells.place: A stone in the Vāsitahamuni temple, built into the wall near the entrance doorway.
cells.date: Vikrama 1394, Vaiśākha śu. 10, Thursday = 1338 A.D., April 30.
cells.remarks: Contains a eulogy of Mahādēva-pādhi, son of Sarasvatī and Gopāla and who is described as a devotee of Śrī Vasiṣṭha. Records that Mahādēva-pādhi caused to be constructed a temple (dharmāyatana) for Vasiṣṭhha. Also records the grant of the villages Jhāṁbhāṇu, Jyotiligrāma and Tējāpura by Rāja-śrī Tējasiṁha of the Chāhamāna-jñāti; of the village Vira-vādāgrāma by Dēvadāsi-Tihuṇaka; of the village Luhulī, Chhāpuli and Kima by the king; and of the villages Lubhuli, Chhāpuli and Kima by the king; and of the villages Lubhulī, Chhāpuli and Kirāpathu by Rāja-śrī-Sāmatasiṁha of the Chāhu-māna-jñāti to the temple of Vasiṣṭha. Published in Ind. Ant., Vol. II, p. 256; Bhandarkar's List, No. 701.

cells.remarks: States that through the efforts of Khwāja Husain entitled Ni'mat Khān son of the deceased Khwāja Jalālụ'd-Dīn Simnānī (i.e. of Simnān), a desert was transformed into a garden which was called Na'imiyya, and a water-channel was excavated and the whole was endowed by him for the general public and their animals for drinking purposes (only). It further prohibits its sale or bestowal as present or mortgage or hire or loan or use as residence, or its fragmenta- tion or alteration. Further says that the trusteeship of the two will vest in his offspring. Written by Muhammad Husain. Cf. Ibid., 1935-36, pp. 37-38, pl. XXV (a).
